issues.legal_issue: A grant expressed to be of a named inam village is treated as a grant of an estate unless the party challenging that treatment proves the relevant exception concerning minor inams.
material_facts: The register described the grant as an agraharam of a named village and recorded its extent in local measures.
A minor inam existed, but there was no evidence establishing when it had been granted or whether it had been carved out of the original grant.
The party contending that the village was not an estate did not discharge its burden of proof.
An earlier judgment, which had the original grant before it, had held the village to be an estate; the village had also been notified as an estate under the abolition legislation.
issues.conclusion: The village was an estate within the meaning of Section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act; the party disputing that status failed to rebut the statutory presumption.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(2)(d), Explanation (1), proof that an inam grant was expressed to be of a named village raises a presumption that the granted area is an estate, including despite certain lands having been granted earlier or reserved for communal purposes. The burden falls on the party asserting that the grant falls outside the definition to establish the relevant exception, including by showing that minor inams not comprised in the grant were created contemporaneously with or after the village grant by the original grantor. Explanation (1-A), inserted by Act XXXV of 1956, confirms that an inam village, hamlet, or khandriga remains an estate even if confirmed or recognised on different dates, under different title deeds, or in favour of different persons. The Court relied on Aluru Kondayya v. Singaraju Rama Rao, approving Nelluru Sundararama Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh, State of Andhra Pradesh v. Korukonda Bhattam Appalacharyulu, Janakiramaraju v. Appalaswami, and Sri Varadarajaswamivari Temple v. Sri Krishnappa Govinda.

predicates.named_village_inam_grant: The grant was expressed to be an inam grant of a named village.
predicates.challenger_proved_minor_inam_exception: The party disputing estate status proved that the relevant minor inams were created contemporaneously with or after the village grant by the original grantor.
predicates.village_treated_as_estate: The village is treated as an estate.

issues.definition: When a grant is expressed to be of a named inam village, the village is treated as an estate if the challenger has not proved the relevant minor-inam exception.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court should not displace a lower appellate court's evidence-based finding in second appeal merely because it takes a different view of the evidence.
material_facts: The lower appellate court assessed documentary evidence and the circumstances and found that the village was an estate.
The High Court reversed that finding in second appeal, misread the register's entry of the extent in local measures, and proceeded on an incorrect allocation of the burden of proof.
The earlier judgment concerning the same village had considered the original grant and reached the same estate-status conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had no justification for interfering with the lower appellate court's finding; the appeals were allowed and the lower appellate court's judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In a second appeal, the High Court was not justified in interfering with the lower appellate court's evidence-based finding merely because it might take a different view of the evidence. The judgment applies this principle to the lower appellate court's assessment of the evidence and the proper allocation of the burden of proof; it cites no separate provision or earlier case for this aspect of the ruling.

predicates.second_appeal: The matter came before a higher court in a second appeal from a lower appellate decision.
predicates.lower_appellate_evidence_finding: The lower appellate court assessed documentary evidence and the circumstances before making its finding.
predicates.higher_court_reversed_on_different_view: The higher court reversed that finding on its own view of the evidence.
predicates.second_appeal_interference_unjustified: The higher court's interference with the lower appellate finding is unjustified.

issues.definition: When a higher court in second appeal reverses an evidence-based lower appellate finding on a different view of the evidence, that interference is unjustified.
